title: sdlc-supervisor task packet
description: The entire scope contract handed from the orchestrator to an implementer for one task. Generated by scripts/generate-task-packet.mjs into .sdlc/task-packets/<task_id>.packet.json. This replaces a vaguer 'list of files it should probably touch' -- read_paths/write_paths/forbidden_paths are the actual scope boundary an implementer (and the path-enforcement hook) is expected to honor.

task_id.description: Task identifier, e.g. 'SS0.3'. Matches the id used in .sdlc/state.json's work_items[].tasks[].

plan_revision.description: Identifies exactly which version of the source implementation-plan entry this packet was generated from, so a later plan edit doesn't silently invalidate an in-flight packet without anyone noticing. Convention: the short git commit SHA of the implementation-plan file at generation time if the repo is clean and the file is tracked/committed, otherwise the string 'uncommitted:<ISO-8601 generation timestamp>' as an honest fallback. Not required to be a git SHA by this schema -- any non-empty string identifying the plan revision is valid.

objective.description: What this task is trying to accomplish, in prose. Generated from the plan entry's own text (and design excerpt, if given), not re-derived.

non_goals.description: Explicit call-outs of adjacent things this task should NOT do. May be empty if the source text doesn't state any -- the generator does not invent non-goals it can't ground in the input text.

dependencies.description: Task IDs (matching other packets' task_id) that must be done before this one can start.

read_paths.description: Path globs the implementer is expected to need to read. Inferred heuristically by the generator -- see the heuristic documented in scripts/generate-task-packet.mjs's header comment. May contain the literal placeholder 'NEEDS_MANUAL_REVIEW' (as its own array entry) when nothing concrete could be inferred from the input text; a packet containing that placeholder is NOT actually ready to hand to an implementer and needs a human/orchestrator pass first.

write_paths.description: Path globs the implementer is expected to need to create or modify. Same inference heuristic and NEEDS_MANUAL_REVIEW convention as read_paths.

forbidden_paths.description: Path globs explicitly off-limits for this task even if they'd otherwise look related (e.g. a sibling in-flight task's files, or production-branch-only files like .sdlc/state.json itself). Not inferred from task text by the generator's heuristic -- populated from project.yaml's always_forbidden_paths plus anything the caller passes explicitly, since 'what NOT to touch' is exactly the kind of thing free text tends not to mention.

acceptance_criteria.description: Human-readable pass/fail conditions this task must satisfy, taken from the plan entry's own acceptance-criteria text when present.

verification_commands.description: Shell commands the implementer (or a verifier) should run to check the work, e.g. this project's own test/build/typecheck commands. May be empty if the source text names none -- the generator does not invent commands it can't ground in the input.

expected_report.description: Fixed pointer to the completion-report schema every implementer's report for this packet must validate against. A constant rather than free text, since there is exactly one report shape in this framework.

max_attempts.description: Maximum number of attempts before this task escalates to the orchestrator instead of being retried automatically. The generator defaults this from project.yaml's budgets.max_attempts_per_task when available, else a hardcoded fallback documented in the generator script.
